versions table that gives each milestone its one version, the features and
epics each milestone delivers, and each milestone's delivery status. No other
skill writes it — `/acs:create-prd` defines the features, this skill schedules
them. It is a **ticketless run** and the document stays an uncommitted change
in the working tree: no ticket, no branch, no commit, no PR (ADR-0127).
`/acs:create-pr "<what changed>"` commits it and opens the PR when the user is
ready.

You orchestrate three subagents — surveyor → author → reviewer — and never
write the roadmap's content yourself. The one change you make to it directly is
the delivery status, and only through `acs.py roadmap status --write`: status is


or resumes this checkout's interrupted manage-roadmap run — and the post-hook

`agents` (agent name to spawn per role), `reconcile`, `handoff_summary`,

```bash

```

hook), write the `<task>` and `<result>` there yourself, through `acs.py write`.

(answers, decisions, partial findings) to
`steps/manage-roadmap/handoff-context.md`, then run


2

5	reviewer hold it to this page, and `acs.py roadmap status` rewrites its status.
6	
7	```markdown

9	
10	## Milestones
11	
12	### M1 Booking MVP — v0.1.0
13	
14	- Status: planned
15	- Features: [Online booking](features/online-booking/prd.md), [SMS reminders](features/sms-reminders/prd.md)
16	- Epics: SHOP-12, SHOP-14
17	- Target: 2027-03-31
18	
19	Why this milestone, and what a user can do once it ships — one paragraph.
20	
21	### M2 Deposits — v0.2.0
22	
23	- Status: planned
24	- Features: [Deposits](features/deposits/prd.md)
25	- Epics: none yet
26	
27	...
28	
29	## Release versions
30	
31	| Version | Milestone | Epics | Status |
32	|---|---|---|---|
33	| v0.1.0 | M1 Booking MVP | SHOP-12, SHOP-14 | planned |
34	| v0.2.0 | M2 Deposits | — | planned |
35	```
36	
37	## The rules
38	
39	- **Milestones** are `###` headings under `## Milestones`, each ending `— v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`:
40	  the release version that is its home. Two milestones never share a version.
41	- **Features** link the feature PRDs the milestone delivers
42	  (`features/<slug>/prd.md`, relative to `roadmap.md`) — every one must exist.
43	  Every **Must-have** feature of the hub's index is in some milestone; a
44	  **Won't-have** feature is in none. A feature may span milestones (an MVP
45	  slice, then the rest): say which part in the paragraph.
46	- **Epics** name the epic tickets that deliver the milestone, or `none yet`.
47	  `/acs:create-ticket` mints them later; the roadmap never invents an id.
48	- **Target** is optional: a date the user gave, never one the author guessed.
49	- **Release versions** has one row per milestone — the same version, the same
50	  milestone name (the heading without its version), its epics, its status — so
51	  every committed milestone resolves to exactly one release version (0 orphan
52	  milestones) and no row names a milestone that is not there.
53	  `/acs:release` never reads this table to resolve tickets; it is for readers.
54	- **Status** is `planned`, `in progress` or `delivered`, and is **derived**,
55	  never written by hand: `acs.py roadmap status --write` reads the tickets each
56	  milestone tracks (its epics, and every ticket linking one of its features)
57	  from the tickets index and the default branch's history, and rewrites only the
58	  Status lines and cells. A new milestone starts `planned`.
59	
60	## Versions
61	
62	The roadmap carries the version front matter (ADR-0122, ADR-0130), set only by
63	the coordinator through `acs.py design`. A run that changes the plan — a
64	milestone added, moved, re-scoped or cut — is one version (`design bump`); a
65	status refresh alone is not a new version and moves no front matter, because
66	the status is a reading of the tickets, not a decision about the plan.

1	# /acs:manage-roadmap — the roadmap document (ADR-0145)
2	
3	`roadmap.md` sits beside the PRD hub (`<prd_dir>/roadmap.md`) and is written by
4	this skill alone. The author writes it, the floor (`roadmap_check.py`) and the
5	reviewer hold it to this page, and `acs.py roadmap status` rewrites its status.
6	
7	```markdown
8	# Roadmap — <product>
9	
10	## Milestones
11	
12	### M1 Booking MVP — v0.1.0
13	
14	- Status: planned
15	- Features: [Online booking](features/online-booking/prd.md), [SMS reminders](features/sms-reminders/prd.md)
16	- Epics: SHOP-12, SHOP-14
17	- Target: 2027-03-31
18	
19	Why this milestone, and what a user can do once it ships — one paragraph.
20	
21	### M2 Deposits — v0.2.0
22	
23	- Status: planned
24	- Features: [Deposits](features/deposits/prd.md)
25	- Epics: none yet
26	
27	...
28	
29	## Release versions
30	
31	| Version | Milestone | Epics | Status |
32	|---|---|---|---|
33	| v0.1.0 | M1 Booking MVP | SHOP-12, SHOP-14 | planned |
34	| v0.2.0 | M2 Deposits | — | planned |
35	```
36	
37	## The rules
38	
39	- **Milestones** are `###` headings under `## Milestones`, each ending `— v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`:
40	  the release version that is its home. Two milestones never share a version.
41	- **Features** link the feature PRDs the milestone delivers
42	  (`features/<slug>/prd.md`, relative to `roadmap.md`) — every one must exist.
43	  Every **Must-have** feature of the hub's index is in some milestone; a
44	  **Won't-have** feature is in none. A feature may span milestones (an MVP
45	  slice, then the rest): say which part in the paragraph.
46	- **Epics** name the epic tickets that deliver the milestone, or `none yet`.
47	  `/acs:create-ticket` mints them later; the roadmap never invents an id.
48	- **Target** is optional: a date the user gave, never one the author guessed.
49	- **Release versions** has one row per milestone — the same version, the same
50	  milestone name (the heading without its version), its epics, its status — so
51	  every committed milestone resolves to exactly one release version (0 orphan
52	  milestones) and no row names a milestone that is not there.
53	  `/acs:release` never reads this table to resolve tickets; it is for readers.
54	- **Status** is `planned`, `in progress` or `delivered`, and is **derived**,
55	  never written by hand: `acs.py roadmap status --write` reads the tickets each
56	  milestone tracks (its epics, and every ticket linking one of its features)
57	  from the tickets index and the default branch's history, and rewrites only the
58	  Status lines and cells. A new milestone starts `planned`.
59	
60	## Versions
61	
62	The roadmap carries the version front matter (ADR-0122, ADR-0130), set only by
63	the coordinator through `acs.py design`. A run that changes the plan — a
64	milestone added, moved, re-scoped or cut — is one version (`design bump`); a
65	status refresh alone is not a new version and moves no front matter, because
66	the status is a reading of the tickets, not a decision about the plan.
67

3	The surveyor writes `steps/manage-roadmap/iter-1/authoring.md`; the author
4	completes it after writing `roadmap.md` and carries it forward as

7	
8	- **`## Mode & evidence`** — `create`, `amend` or `replan`, and why: whether
9	  `roadmap.md` exists (path), and for `replan` the drift that calls for it (a
10	  feature cut, added or re-prioritised in the PRD, quoted with its line).
11	- **`## PRD features`** — the hub's Features index as the surveyor read it, one
12	  line per feature: `- <slug> — <Must|Should|Could|Won't> — supports G1, G3`,
13	  each with the `prd.md` line it rests on. A feature PRD that does not exist is
14	  recorded as such, never invented.
15	- **`## Delivery evidence`** — the output of `acs.py roadmap status` (never
16	  `--write` — the surveyor is read-only), quoted: each milestone's derived status
17	  and the tickets behind it; the epics the tickets index holds that link one of
18	  the PRD's features. No roadmap yet: `none — create mode`.
19	- **`## Roadmap outline`** — the plan: every milestone with its name, version,
20	  features (slugs), epics (ids, or `none yet`), target (only one the user gave)
21	  and its one-paragraph why. In amend/replan mode, mark each milestone `kept`
22	  (byte-for-byte), `changed` (what and why) or `new`, and list each one cut.
23	- **`## Roadmap milestones`** — the floor's grammar: one line per milestone of
24	  the outline, quoting its heading text without the `###`:
25	
26	  ```
27	  - Milestone: "M1 Booking MVP — v0.1.0"
28	  ```
29	
30	- **`## Answer fidelity`** — one line per `answered`/`assumed` entry of
31	  `clarifications.json`: `- C-<n> — roadmap.md — "<verbatim anchor>"`, or
32	  `- C-<n> N/A: <why this answer produces no anchor>`. The surveyor names the
33	  answers the ledger already holds; the author adds the rest and completes every
34	  anchor against the text it wrote. Every ledger id appears exactly once.
35	- **`## Open questions`** — what only the user can settle: the order of
36	  milestones, which feature ships first, a version, a target date. Never a fact
37	  the PRD, the tickets or the code already answer.
38	- **`## Deviations`** — the author's: each change to the outline, with the
39	  answer (`C-<n>`) or finding that drove it. From iteration 2, **`## Findings
40	  addressed`** maps each reviewer finding to the change that fixed it.
41	
42	**What the floor checks** (`roadmap_check.py`, rules in its docstring): the
43	roadmap's own shape against `roadmap-shape.md` and the hub's index (every rule,
44	every mode); with `--plan`, the notes' `## Roadmap milestones` against the
